trigger: aggregate_responses (MCP, mcp_server.cpp) and GET /api/v1/responses/{id}/aggregate (REST, rest_api_v1.cpp) both assign the RAW (possibly-empty) op_column value to AggregationQuery::op_column instead of the validated effective_op_column local, relying on ResponseStore::aggregate() (response_store.cpp:863) to independently re-derive the same empty->"id" default
summary: No functional bug today (both defaults agree), but the two defaults are independent implementations that could silently diverge on a future edit to either one -- exactly the false-degrade shape #2691 exists to prevent. Fixed in this pass: both call sites now assign effective_op_column, not the raw optional/param. A regression test was added asserting omitted op_column produces the identical aggregate result as explicit op_column:"id", which would fail if the two defaults ever drift.
classification_rationale: the code silently substitutes a raw un-normalized value where the store contract expects the normalized default -- correct today only by coincidental agreement between two independent implementations of the same default, which is itself the contradiction the finding names

summary: cpp-expert's own label was SHOULD/track-not-block (severity_native), but the derived band from the stated facts (I3+E3) is HIGH/BLOCKING -- the derived band governs the gate per the shared severity rubric, so severity_mapped is recorded as BLOCKING despite the reporter's softer native label. Initially proposed as a deferred follow-up (issue #4643 filed), but re-derivation against the severity rubric shows this is genuinely I3 (wrong result silently substituted and presented as correct) at E3 (any authenticated operator, default config) -> HIGH, which the ledger's own park-probe correctly refuses to let through with a roadmap/linked-to disposition. Fixed directly in this pass instead: `aggregate` now uses param_string_strict, mirroring op_column's fix exactly (same PR, same commit). Issue #4643 closed as fixed rather than left open. A well-typed-but-unrecognized aggregate string (e.g. "bogus") still falls through to "count" unchanged, matching the legacy route's identical behavior -- that narrower enum-validation gap is a separate, genuinely lower-severity (E6-capped, security-guardian's own NICE note) pre-existing issue and remains out of scope.
classification_rationale: the tool's declared input schema states aggregate is a typed enum string; the implementation's actual behavior (silently substituting the default on any wrong-typed value) contradicts that declared contract
